convoLines.text: "Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"This one — Jujube. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held."
"Still on what you believe in."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." I counted the stores twice today. We need more. We always need more.
"Food's the first promise a group makes to itself: we won't let each other starve."
"I'd rather be the cook than the hero. Heroes get songs. Cooks get everyone through winter."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Ashley?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."

"It's my grandmother, Ashley. Was taken. Eighty-one years old and they called her boring. Eighty-one years. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Keisha always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on what you miss most."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Keisha is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I do push-ups at dawn at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Nobody says Keisha's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them American Persimmon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About what happened to my taken kin — I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Still nothing on Ashley. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Keisha died... I keep expecting to see Keisha at the fire. Stupid."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
They give you the benefit of the doubt. This time.
"Still on your read on people here."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I put down The Living Wire at the treeline. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About what happened to my taken kin — Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
They nod. "Okay."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Rest when you can."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "That night — I stood down Rut King at the treeline — it ran. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are. Anyway, I should move."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some American Persimmon today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took me. The Exchange — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Tell me — I tried the Mayapple like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Andres doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Eduardo and Axel — The Exchange, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Keisha Xi is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Keisha Xi is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Keisha — and Keisha is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d42: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. tick is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Keisha home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Andres, Eduardo, Axel and 4 more speak for Catalina — "Keisha trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d43: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
